scenes.tts: The first film fixed the codon boxes. How does each box choose an amino acid? Keep the same blue message, gold start, and teal reading window. Now add the adaptor that connects sequence to protein.
scenes.caption: The first film fixed the codon boxes. How does each box choose an amino acid? Keep the same blue message, gold start, and teal reading window. Now add the adaptor that connects sequence to protein.
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's exact sixteen-by-nine world and COLOUR MAP: mRNA and codons BLUE; start and fixed register GOLD; reading window and ribosome action TEAL; amino acids and peptide GREEN; stops RED; tRNA YELLOW; unresolved states GREY. Carry in the BLUE ribbon, GOLD start, and TEAL window from the first film. A GREEN amino-acid block hovers above one codon with a GREY question mark between them. Keep 'schematic' at lower right.
scenes.narration: The first film fixed the codon boxes. How does each box choose an amino acid? Keep the same blue message, gold start, and teal reading window. Now add the adaptor that connects sequence to protein.

scenes.visual: Over the carried BLUE ribbon and YELLOW tRNA, show the title 'How Codons Become a Chain' for two seconds. The TEAL reading window glides and the GREEN cargo block bobs gently; keep 'schematic' at lower right.

scenes.tts: A transfer R N A has two working ends. Its anticodon can pair with a codon. Its other end carries an amino acid. The adaptor keeps both identities physically linked as it moves.
scenes.caption: A transfer RNA has two working ends. Its anticodon can pair with a codon. Its other end carries an amino acid. The adaptor keeps both identities physically linked as it moves.
scenes.visual: A large YELLOW L-shaped tRNA cartoon grows to fill most of the frame. Label the lower tip 'anticodon' and the upper tip 'amino-acid end'. A BLUE codon strip slides under the anticodon while a GREEN cargo block settles on top. The two labels stay attached as the adaptor rocks gently.
scenes.narration: A transfer RNA has two working ends. Its anticodon can pair with a codon. Its other end carries an amino acid. The adaptor keeps both identities physically linked as it moves.

scenes.tts: Before the adaptor reaches a ribosome, an aminoacyl transfer R N A synthetase usually loads it. The enzyme selects an amino acid and the transfer R N A meant to carry it. Some synthetases also remove mistakes.
scenes.caption: Before the adaptor reaches a ribosome, an aminoacyl transfer RNA synthetase usually loads it. The enzyme selects an amino acid and the transfer RNA meant to carry it. Some synthetases also remove mistakes.
scenes.visual: A TEAL clamp labelled 'synthetase' closes around the upper end of the YELLOW tRNA and one GREEN amino-acid block. Several wrong GREEN blocks approach, then move away without labels implying absolute rejection. The selected block attaches; a small path labelled 'editing may remove errors' opens beside the clamp.
scenes.narration: Before the adaptor reaches a ribosome, an aminoacyl transfer RNA synthetase usually loads it. The enzyme selects an amino acid and the transfer RNA meant to carry it. Some synthetases also remove mistakes.

scenes.tts: Translation therefore depends on separate checks. The synthetase chooses the cargo. At the ribosome, the anticodon tests the codon. The growing chain receives whatever cargo arrived on the accepted adaptor. Charged transfer R N As connect codons to the growing protein.
scenes.caption: Translation therefore depends on separate checks. The synthetase chooses the cargo. At the ribosome, the anticodon tests the codon. The growing chain receives whatever cargo arrived on the accepted adaptor. Charged transfer RNAs connect codons to the growing protein.
scenes.visual: Split the carried world into two connected stations, not separate cards. At left, the TEAL synthetase loads a GREEN block onto YELLOW tRNA. The charged adaptor travels along a curved path to the TEAL ribosome window at right, where its anticodon aligns with a BLUE codon. A thin GOLD arrow connects 'charge' to 'pair'.
scenes.narration: Translation therefore depends on separate checks. The synthetase chooses the cargo. At the ribosome, the anticodon tests the codon. The growing chain receives whatever cargo arrived on the accepted adaptor. Charged transfer RNAs connect codons to the growing protein.

scenes.tts: Predict this case. A transfer R N A carries the wrong amino acid, but its anticodon matches the codon. Will the ribosome reject the adaptor, or accept it?
scenes.caption: Predict this case. A transfer RNA carries the wrong amino acid, but its anticodon matches the codon. Will the ribosome reject the adaptor, or accept it?
scenes.visual: Show a YELLOW tRNA with an anticodon matching the BLUE codon. Its cargo is a GREEN block labelled 'wrong amino acid'. The adaptor waits outside the TEAL A-site slot. Put 'reject?' and 'accept?' on opposite sides while the matching bases pulse.
scenes.narration: Predict this case. A transfer RNA carries the wrong amino acid, but its anticodon matches the codon. Will the ribosome reject the adaptor, or accept it?

scenes.visual: Deliberate prediction pause. Keep the matching anticodon and wrong cargo visible, with 'reject?' and 'accept?' unchanged. A thin GOLD ring completes one slow turn; do not move the adaptor into the ribosome yet.

scenes.tts: The pairing check passes. The ribosome does not inspect the amino acid itself. The wrong cargo can enter the chain. Accuracy therefore depends on charging before the ribosome and pairing at the ribosome.
scenes.caption: The pairing check passes. The ribosome does not inspect the amino acid itself. The wrong cargo can enter the chain. Accuracy therefore depends on charging before the ribosome and pairing at the ribosome.
scenes.visual: Move the matching anticodon into the TEAL A-site slot. The 'accept' label brightens, but use no celebratory checkmark. Transfer the wrong-labelled GREEN block onto a schematic peptide. Then rewind to the charging station and highlight both checkpoints together, showing where accuracy must be protected.
scenes.narration: The pairing check passes. The ribosome does not inspect the amino acid itself. The wrong cargo can enter the chain. Accuracy therefore depends on charging before the ribosome and pairing at the ribosome.

scenes.tts: Now follow a cycle. The pee site holds the transfer R N A carrying the growing chain. The ay site receives a charged adaptor whose anticodon matches the next codon. The ee site is the exit.
scenes.caption: Now follow a cycle. The P site holds the transfer RNA carrying the growing chain. The A site receives a charged adaptor whose anticodon matches the next codon. The E site is the exit.
scenes.visual: Build one large TEAL ribosome cartoon around the BLUE ribbon. Place three big slots labelled E, P, and A from left to right. Put the YELLOW chain-bearing tRNA in P with a GREEN chain. Bring a charged YELLOW tRNA into A. Keep E empty but moving faintly to cue the exit.
scenes.narration: Now follow a cycle. The P site holds the transfer RNA carrying the growing chain. The A site receives a charged adaptor whose anticodon matches the next codon. The E site is the exit.

scenes.tts: The large subunit transfers the chain onto the amino acid in the ay site. Then the ribosome advances by a codon. The chain-bearing adaptor moves into the pee site, while the empty adaptor reaches the ee site and leaves.
scenes.caption: The large subunit transfers the chain onto the amino acid in the A site. Then the ribosome advances by a codon. The chain-bearing adaptor moves into the P site, while the empty adaptor reaches the E site and leaves.
scenes.visual: Swing the GREEN chain from the P-site tRNA onto the GREEN amino acid in A. Slide the BLUE ribbon left by exactly one codon while the TEAL ribosome stays centered. Move the new chain-bearing tRNA from A to P; move the empty tRNA from P to E and out.
scenes.narration: The large subunit transfers the chain onto the amino acid in the A site. Then the ribosome advances by a codon. The chain-bearing adaptor moves into the P site, while the empty adaptor reaches the E site and leaves.

scenes.tts: The ribosome is not merely a track. Its large-subunit R N A positions the two transfer R N A ends and catalyzes peptide-bond formation. The reaction occurs in an R N A-lined pocket. That is why the ribosome is called a ribozyme.
scenes.caption: The ribosome is not merely a track. Its large-subunit RNA positions the two transfer RNA ends and catalyzes peptide-bond formation. The reaction occurs in an RNA-lined pocket. That is why the ribosome is called a ribozyme.
scenes.visual: Keep one large TEAL ribosome cartoon around the BLUE ribbon. Highlight a broad region in the large subunit labelled 'RNA-lined pocket'. Bring the two GREEN reacting ends together as labelled blocks, without atoms, bonds, or molecular structures. Pulse the label 'ribozyme', then return the chain and tRNAs to the carried layout.
scenes.narration: The ribosome is not merely a track. Its large-subunit RNA positions the two transfer RNA ends and catalyzes peptide-bond formation. The reaction occurs in an RNA-lined pocket. That is why the ribosome is called a ribozyme.

scenes.tts: The same blue ribbon moves through the teal window. Each accepted adaptor adds a green block, so the chain grows in codon order. The ribosome repeats the cycle without changing the frame.
scenes.caption: The same blue ribbon moves through the teal window. Each accepted adaptor adds a green block, so the chain grows in codon order. The ribosome repeats the cycle without changing the frame.
scenes.visual: Run two more smooth cycles on the carried world. Each YELLOW tRNA arrives, pairs, transfers one GREEN block, shifts through P and E, and leaves. Keep the GOLD start and triplet brackets visible so the frame never changes. The chain lengthens across most of the frame.
scenes.narration: The same blue ribbon moves through the teal window. Each accepted adaptor adds a green block, so the chain grows in codon order. The ribosome repeats the cycle without changing the frame.

scenes.tts: When a stop enters the ay site, a release factor arrives instead of a transfer R N A. The completed chain leaves, and the ribosome can be recycled. The stop adds no amino acid.
scenes.caption: When a stop enters the A site, a release factor arrives instead of a transfer RNA. The completed chain leaves, and the ribosome can be recycled. The stop adds no amino acid.
scenes.visual: A RED stop codon slides into A. Replace the incoming YELLOW tRNA with a simple RED block labelled 'release factor'. Lift the completed GREEN chain away without adding a block. The TEAL ribosome separates into two schematic subunit blocks, ready to reset.
scenes.narration: When a stop enters the A site, a release factor arrives instead of a transfer RNA. The completed chain leaves, and the ribosome can be recycled. The stop adds no amino acid.

scenes.tts: The codon never touches its amino acid directly. A charged adaptor makes the connection, while the ribosome preserves the order. The adaptor carries identity from the code to the chain.
scenes.caption: The codon never touches its amino acid directly. A charged adaptor makes the connection, while the ribosome preserves the order. The adaptor carries identity from the code to the chain.
scenes.visual: Arrange the final carried objects in one continuous path: BLUE codon, paired YELLOW anticodon, YELLOW tRNA, GREEN cargo, and GREEN growing chain inside the TEAL ribosome. A GOLD pulse travels once from codon to chain. Then fade all objects together before the end card.
scenes.narration: The codon never touches its amino acid directly. A charged adaptor makes the connection, while the ribosome preserves the order. The adaptor carries identity from the code to the chain.

scenes.visual: Clear everything. Show one line only, centered in large high-contrast type: 'Charged tRNAs connect codons to the growing protein.' No subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
